# /add-language — scaffold a new instance language engineer (fill-in-the-blanks)

Order-enforcing scaffold. A new instance language needs a scoped engineer persona, a `project.toml`
registration, and a matching permission scope — and the GEN-03 consistency gate
(`tools/harness_lint/tests/test_language_config.py`) fails if any of the three disagree. This macro
walks the three edits so they stay consistent. The language id/toolchain comes from `$ARGUMENTS`.

The engineer is a **derivation of the neutral template**, not a hand-authored persona: the core
ships `harness/agents/templates/engineer.md`, and `python-engineer` is its reference instantiation.
This is what makes "a second instance language gets a fill-in-the-blanks engineer" actually true.

## Mandated order (keep the three in sync)

1. **Derive the persona from the template.** Copy `harness/agents/templates/engineer.md` into the
   active instance's own `agents/` directory (the instance root is declared by
   `harness/project.toml [instance] root`) as `<lang>-engineer.md`. Fill every `<PLACEHOLDER>`:
   `<LANG>`, `<TOOLCHAIN>`, `<TEST_CMD>`, `<BASH_SCOPE>`. The persona lands in the **instance**, not
   the core — so the core persona anti-sprawl set stays fixed.

2. **Register the language in `project.toml`.** Append a `[[languages]]` table with `id`,
   `bash_scope`, `test`, optional `format`/`sdk_bootstrap`, and `persona = "<instance>/agents/<lang>-engineer.md"`.
   The `persona` and `root` lines are the ONE sanctioned place a core-plane file may name an
   instance path (ADR-0002 (c)) — the drift guard exempts exactly those lines.

3. **Add the matching bash scope to the permission matrix.** Add `"<BASH_SCOPE>": "allow"` to the
   `bash` object in `harness/permission-matrix.json`, keeping the catch-all `*` FIRST and the
   specific scope after (last-wins glob, Pitfall P3). The persona's `<BASH_SCOPE>` allow and this
   matrix scope MUST match — that agreement is what `test_language_config.py` (GEN-03) asserts.

## Guard

- **All three or none.** A persona whose `bash_scope` is not in the matrix, or a `project.toml` row
  whose `persona` file is missing, red-flags the GEN-03 consistency gate. Make the three edits
  together, then run `/test`.
- **Least privilege.** The new engineer allows only its own `<BASH_SCOPE>`; everything else stays
  `ask`. Do not grant a broad bash allow.
- **Domain-neutral core stays neutral.** The derived persona and its content live in the instance;
  the core template must not gain instance/domain vocabulary.
- Validate the persona/template shape against the same rules the core personas follow (subagent
  mode, valid permission keys, routing description) before committing.
